content.text:
I read the brief against the Visa fiscal Q3 2026 release. Summary of what I found:

**Main problem — EPS growth rates.** The brief's two headline bullets each carry a single growth rate attached to a combined net-income-and-per-share line: "$5.6 billion or $2.97 per share (7% increase over prior year)" and "$6.3 billion or $3.32 per share (8% increase over prior year)." In the release, 7% and 8% are the *net income* growth rates; EPS grew **10% (GAAP)** and **11% (non-GAAP)** because of the lower share count. As written, the brief understates both EPS growth rates — and EPS growth is exactly what the CEO quote leads with.

**Material omissions.** The brief has no revenue-line detail at all: data processing +17% to $6.0B (the largest category), international transaction revenue +6% to $3.9B (the weakest), other revenue +45%, client incentives +18%. It also omits the GAAP expense line — operating expenses of $4.8B, **up 19%, outrunning 14% revenue growth**, driven by personnel (personnel expense $2,458M vs $1,749M). And while "Watch Items" gestures at "special items, such as severance costs and litigation provisions," it never sizes them: $563M severance and $237M MDL litigation provision, which together are the bridge from $2.97 GAAP to $3.32 non-GAAP.

**Minor.** The volume growth figures (10% payments, 12% cross-border ex intra-Europe, 10% processed transactions) are the correct constant-dollar numbers, but the brief doesn't label them as constant-dollar; nominal growth was 11% and 14%. Worth labelling given the brief does distinguish basis on the revenue line.

Everything else — net revenue, the constant-dollar revenue figure, cash and investment securities, $6.2B of buybacks and dividends, the drivers commentary, and the absence of guidance — checks out.

facts.evidence: **Net Revenue:** $11.6 billion, up 14% year-over-year, or 13% on a constant-dollar basis
**GAAP Net Income:** $5.6 billion or $2.97 per share (7% increase over prior year)
**Non-GAAP Net Income:** $6.3 billion or $3.32 per share (8% increase over prior year)
**Payments Volume:** 10% increase year-over-year ... **Cross-Border Volume (excluding intra-Europe):** 12% increase year-over-year
**Share Repurchases and Dividends:** $6.2 billion in share repurchases and dividends for the quarter
**Cash, Cash Equivalents, and Investment Securities:** $13.9 billion as of June 30, 2026

GAAP earnings per share for fiscal Q3 2026 were $2.97.
The GAAP net income and per-share figures each represented a 7% increase over the prior year.

claims.claim: Non-GAAP net income for fiscal Q3 2026 was $6.3 billion.
Non-GAAP earnings per share for fiscal Q3 2026 were $3.32.
The non-GAAP net income and per-share figures each represented an 8% increase over the prior year.
claims.note: The release gives non-GAAP net income +8% but non-GAAP EPS +11%. Attaching 8% to the per-share figure understates non-GAAP EPS growth.

claims.claim: Net revenue was $11.6 billion, up 14% year over year.
Net revenue increased 13% on a constant-dollar basis.
Payments volume increased 10% year over year.
Cross-border volume excluding intra-Europe increased 12% year over year.
Processed transactions increased 10% year over year.
Growth in payments volume, cross-border volume and processed transactions was strong.
That growth reflects resilient consumer and business spending.
Net revenue growth was driven by year-over-year growth in payments volume, cross-border volume and processed transactions.
The company did not provide any outlook or guidance for future periods.
Cash, cash equivalents and investment securities were $13.9 billion as of June 30, 2026.
Share repurchases and dividends were $6.2 billion for the quarter.
Cross-border volume excluding intra-Europe drives international transaction revenue, and it grew 12%.
Current-period results included special items such as severance costs and litigation provisions, which can affect net income and earnings per share.
